purpose.summary: Guidance for designing web banners in the Bosch Corporate Design.
purpose.implementation_context: Full implementation requires basic understanding of the Core and the general design principles of the Digital Design System.

topics.role: Defines the grid structure for web banner composition.
Defines spacing relationships and visual rhythm.
Defines composition and placement principles for banner elements.
Provides correct and incorrect usage examples.

rules: The web banner layout is based on a predefined baseline grid and a variable column grid. This allows a flexible component placement while keeping consistent spacings.

Baseline grid: All components are aligned along a square 0.25 rem (4 px) baseline grid. The spacing between each line can be easily defined in increments of rem (0.5 rem, 1 rem, 2 rem, 3 rem). Padding: Horizontal and vertical spacing within the Brand Area, i.e. between supergraphic bar, symbol/logotype and content, as well as from content to Experience Area (product image). Padding depends on the web banner size, the structure within the brand/experience layer as well as the content density.
The Bosch Digital Design System provides predefined spacing throughout components and also between the components for easier layout work. Learn more on general spacing

Banners are following the Bosch Layout Principle consisting of two flexible areas: Brand Area: The Brand Area offers room for the Bosch Brand and always contains at least the Supergraphic, symbol / logotype and slogan. Experience Area: The Experience Area contains images, colors or illustrations.

The Bosch Layout Principle for web banners The versatility of the Bosch Layout Principle has been optimized for the small space offered in banners. The goal is to achieve good legibility on the small surface area within the image section. Therefore, specific rules apply here: The text can be placed either on the Brand Area or within an additional content tile on Experience Area. The text may not be placed without a tile (on the Experience Area). The placement and size of Supergraphic and Symbol / logotype is predefined within the web banner template and must not be changed. Furthermore, the existing rules still apply: The relation between the Brand Area and the Experience Area is flexible; an image can be enlarged or minimized depending on the amount of text (rolling shutter principle). The placement of Supergraphic and Symbol / logotype can be varied in the web banner template – top, bottom or left, right. In addition, a solid filled tile can be placed on the experience area to show text. Only one button may be used as a call-to-action on Primary Background. On Major Highlight Background, no button may be used. Instead, a pseudo headline link is mandatory. More info can be found here . Mandatory elements Headline, symbol / logotype & Primary Button (or Headline link) Optional elements Subline, bold copy & image

Billboard: 93.75 × 43.75 rem (1500 × 700 px) Halfpage Ad: 18.75 × 37.5 rem (300 × 600 px) Medium Rectangle: 18.75 × 15.625 rem (300 × 250 px) Skyscraper: 10 × 37.5 rem (160 × 600 px) Wide Leaderboard: 60.625 × 5.625 rem (970 × 90 px)

Special button types are used for the banner design. These are conditioned on the one hand, by the smaller design area and on the other hand, in combination with the adjacent content (headline, subline) to create a balanced overall picture. These differ from the standard core button in the height and the distances before and after the text label.
Minimum spacing between button and slogan: 2rem (32px)
The text is on the Brand Area and can be dragged to any size.
Text is on a "calm" background without white filled tile.
The text must not be placed on a "vivid" background (Experience Area).

dos: Text on Brand Area on calm background
Text can be dragged to any size on Brand Area
donts: Text without white filled tile on vivid Experience Area background
Text placed directly on Experience Area without tile
